# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

# R2 — Harden the audit JSON contract (JSON-first prompt + tolerant extraction + bounded re-ask)

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Genuine JSON-contract failures are rarer than the debug label suggests
(~5-8%), but they are real and avoidable. In real-project logs, 34 genuine
failures; the dominant shape is the model stopping (`stopReason: stop`) after
narrative analysis and never emitting the required JSON array, with 16/34
producing <200 output tokens (empty or truncated text). Pi also routinely
wraps the array in Markdown code fences (```` ```json ... ``` ````) with prose
around it.

Prior art: SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8 (parse mixed analysis+JSON),
SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A (JSON parse fallback), SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC (consolidate Pi
JSON parsers, open).

## Desired change

Make the JSON contract JSON-first and tolerant, and add a single bounded
"return only the JSON array" re-ask before the conservative `partial`
fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 1 parent/child and Phase 2 parent/child prompts request the JSON
   array first (or only), with prose after, and restate the exact schema and
   the required keys.
2. `_extract_json_array` tolerates leading/trailing prose and Markdown code
   fences and selects the intended balanced array; covered by unit tests using
   real fenced/prose fixtures captured from the debug corpus.
3. On extraction failure, exactly one bounded re-ask ("return only the JSON
   array") is issued before falling back to `partial`; the re-ask is
   observable (context `verdict_reask`) and bounded by the per-call budget.
4. A genuine parse-failure rate is measured over a re-run corpus (>=20 items)
   and recorded on this item; it is reduced relative to the pre-change
   baseline.
5. Verdict semantics are unchanged: a persistent failure still falls back to
   the conservative `partial`, never `met`/`Yes`.
6. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- No project-specific commands; use the shared Pi utilities (`skill/scripts/pi_utils.py`)
  rather than adding a new parser (align with SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC).
- Evidence-scope cap (`--max-citations-per-ac`) must remain honoured.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_extract_json_array`, Phase 1/2
  prompts, `verdict_reask` handling.
- `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py` — `extract_pi_text`.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — parser fixtures/tests.
data.title: R2: Harden the audit JSON contract (JSON-first + tolerant extraction + bounded re-ask)

# R7 — Emit a per-run audit reliability summary

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Assessing audit reliability currently requires log archaeology across
`~/.audit_debug/**` and the worklog export (the RCA for
SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL needed bespoke scripts). There is no single per-run
signal an operator can read to see how healthy an audit was.

## Desired change

Emit one machine-greppable reliability summary per `audit_runner.py issue`
run, so future RCAs and dashboards do not need log archaeology.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each `audit_runner.py issue` run emits exactly one summary line (stderr
   and/or appended to the report) with stable, documented keys: calls,
   parse_ok, parse_failed, timeouts, child_skips, provider_errors,
   concurrency_waits, elapsed_seconds.
2. The summary format is documented in `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
3. Tests cover the summary formatting and key stability.
4. The summary is available even when the run ends early (timeout/abort),
   where possible.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **R1** for accurate parse/provider counts; **R6** for provider
  totals.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Must not print secrets/credentials; counts only.
data.title: R7: Emit a per-run audit reliability summary

# Diagnose the shared-state leak

## Goal

Pinpoint the shared-state leak or timing assumption that makes the budget/resume tests fail only in full-repo order, and document the mechanism by which it crosses test boundaries — satisfying AC1 of SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The offending state, environment variable or module is identified, with the mechanism by which it leaks across test boundaries documented.
- Each candidate suspect is explicitly eliminated or confirmed: the `_AUDIT_TICKET_COUNTER` module-level counter, `_apply_proxy_mode_serialization()` `os.environ` writes, the flock-based audit semaphore/queue, and `stateful_wl_side_effect`.
- Confirmation evidence is captured: ordering the suspect test(s) before the module reproduces the failure, and neutralising the leaked state in the harness makes it pass.
- The findings, evidence and elimination table are recorded as a comment on this work item.

## Constraints

- Diagnosis only — no production behaviour changes in this item; the fix belongs in "Implement the isolation fix".
- Distinguish test-order pollution from genuine production bugs; record which side owns the defect.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — module-level state and process-wide mutation.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`, `skill/shared/queue.py` — shared helpers (implicated only if evidence points there).
- `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py` — `stateful_wl_side_effect`, the per-call worklog state model.
data.title: Diagnose the shared-state leak

# Implement the isolation fix

## Goal

Fix the identified root cause so all 5 budget/resume tests pass deterministically in full-repo runs, without masking the flake — satisfying AC2 of SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All 5 tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_budget_exceeded_resume.py` pass across at least 5 consecutive full-repo runs.
- No assertion is weakened, no test is skipped or xfailed, and no retry wrapper is introduced to mask the flake.
- Production semantics are unchanged unless the diagnosis in "Diagnose the shared-state leak" proved production code at fault; if so, the justification is recorded in this work item.
- The change is scoped to the audit test suite, or to a shared helper with full-suite verification.
- A comment records the commit hash and the exact commands run.

## Constraints

- Do not serialise the whole suite, add global sleeps, or run tests in a single worker as the fix.
- Keep the blast radius minimal; verify the full project suite if a shared helper changes.

- `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py`

## Purpose

**Authoritative SorraAgents record** for the nested `node_modules` worktree symlink change. Per the producer decision on 2026-09-26, this item is the authoritative release-tracking record; the open_source_llm item **OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT** is the originating cross-repo record and is subordinated to this item.

## Status

**Already implemented, tested and pushed to SorraAgents `dev` in commit `763b8f11`.**

## Relationship to OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT

- `OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT` and its children — `OSL-0MUGXT9SX008CZU8` (helper + wiring), `OSL-0MUGXTVLT00236M0` (tests), `OSL-0MUGXUPMA005W5HU` (docs + full suite), `OSL-0MUI78ROQ005B37N` (cross-repo `wl` resolution) — are all `completed`/`in_review` in the open_source_llm worklog.
- Per the producer decision (2026-09-26), **this SA item is authoritative**; the OSL item is a cross-repo duplicate/companion and does not independently gate the SorraAgents release.

## What shipped

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks(worktree_path, repo_root) -> int` and `_iter_nested_node_modules(repo_root)`: bounded, best-effort discovery + symlink of nested `node_modules` (e.g. `.pi/packages/<pkg>/node_modules`) into an implement worktree, wired into `phase_start()` immediately after `_ensure_node_modules_symlink()`.
  - `wl_show` / `wl_show_children` / `wl_dep_blockers` / `wl_add_comment` / `_is_work_item_open` now use `resolve_worklog_flags(cmd)` (prefix-to-sibling) instead of `worklog_dir_flag()` (cwd chain), fixing cross-repo `OSL-*` resolution from the SorraAgents checkout.
- `tests/test_implement_nested_node_modules_symlink.py` (AC1-AC7, incl. a Node `require.resolve` check).
- `tests/test_implement_cross_repo_worklog_resolution.py` (6 regression tests).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` documents nested symlinks and retains the no-`npm install`-in-worktree caveat.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Nested `node_modules` symlinks created at the same relative path, resolving to the main checkout (AC2).
- [x] Existing entries never overwritten (AC3); no fabricated package dirs (AC4).
- [x] Bounded discovery: prunes `.git`/`.worklog`, never descends into `node_modules`, never follows symlinks (AC5).
- [x] Per-candidate failures are logged at WARNING, never fatal (AC6).
- [x] Root-level symlink behaviour and tests unchanged (AC1).
- [x] Dedicated helper + automated tests incl. Node resolution check (AC7).
- [x] Docs updated (AC8).
- [x] Full suite green (AC9).

## Current state / gate

- Status `blocked`; stage `plan_complete` (this repo's allowed stages: `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`, `done`).
- Blocked by **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** (GIT_DIR leak). The `in_review` audit fan-out must not run until that critical incident is fixed, because it can re-corrupt the live checkout and `origin/dev`.
- Advance to `in_review` once `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` is fixed, so the SorraAgents release process can close it.
- `needsProducerReview` cleared on 2026-09-26 — the authority decision resolves the open question.
data.title: Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (authoritative record for OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT)
